newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes mostly down, losses trimmed late.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes mostly down, losses trimmed late.

text.p: Early losses were trimmed in WCE canola futures by local and commercial buying sparked partly by a late rally in CBOT soybeans, dealers said.
They noted the market's short-term direction was likely to hinge on the amount of rain in South America over the weekend. Some Brazilian soybean areas have been particularly short of precipitation.
"What happens this weekend in Brazil will likely determine our direction Monday. If it rains we'll likely go down," one WCE trader said.

Crusher buying of new crop months was noted while the recent strength of the Canadian dollar remained a bearish influence on export demand. Japan was reported to have bought 2,000 tonnes of Canadian canola overnight.
Flaxseed fell late under pressure from hedge selling in thin conditions. March ended off $2.90 at $355.30.
Feed grains were lower in very quiet trading.

Western barley volume mainly included rolling forward of positions out of February. In the wheat pit, locals already holding short positions offered down new crop months, taking advantage of the lack of buy-orders in the pit.
March wheat closed $1.30 down at $169.50 and February barley off $0.80 at $136.70.
Feed peas saw light trade in the May contract at lower prices with export-related selling noted. Dealers said UGG was the day's buyer. May closed off US$2.00 at $195.00.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
